mainTopic: End of the משנה on שמחת בית השואבה; the glory of הורדוס's בית המקדש and the synagogue of אלכסנדריא; the balcony separating men and women
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about שמחת בית השואבה on סוכות. Pious men danced with torches, and the לוים played music on the fifteen steps. At dawn, כהנים blew trumpets as the procession went down to draw water. At the eastern gate they turned to face the היכל and declared that their eyes are turned to ה', unlike their ancestors who worshipped the sun. The גמרא praises the celebration, ירושלים and the בית המקדש as rebuilt by הורדוס, whose marble walls looked like the waves of the sea. It then describes the huge synagogue of אלכסנדריא and tells how its community was destroyed by אלכסנדר מוקדון for settling in מצרים. Finally it explains the משנה's 'תיקון גדול': a balcony so the women sat above and the men below. It asks how anyone could change the בית המקדש's divine plan, and רב begins to answer that they learned it from a פסוק, which the next amud quotes.

steps.title: Dancing with torches and singing praises
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues describing the pious men at שמחת בית השואבה, who danced with burning torches and sang songs of praise.
steps.simpleTranslation: With torches of fire in their hands, and they would say before them words of songs and praises.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the משנה in the middle of a sentence. The pious men (חסידים ואנשי מעשה, mentioned on the previous amud) danced holding burning torches and sang praises to ה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is painting a picture of the celebration, not giving a legal rule. The leaders of the people, not just professional singers, were the ones dancing and praising. This shows how central and joyful this event was.

keyTerms.meaning: Before them (in front of the crowd, or before God)

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts mid-sentence. The people holding the torches are the חסידים ואנשי מעשה from the previous line of the משנה.

phrases.english: with torches of fire that were in their hands,
phrases.notes: The גמרא later describes some of them juggling these torches.

phrases.english: and they would say before them
words of songs and praises.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The pious men danced with torches and sang praises at שמחת בית השואבה.

steps.title: The לוים play music on the fifteen steps
steps.stepSummary: The לוים played many instruments while standing on the fifteen steps between עזרת ישראל and עזרת נשים. These steps match the fifteen שיר המעלות chapters in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The לוים played lyres, harps, cymbals, trumpets and countless other instruments. They stood on the fifteen steps going down from עזרת ישראל to עזרת נשים. These correspond to the fifteen שיר המעלות chapters in תהלים, and on them the לוים stand with instruments and sing.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds the musical part of the celebration. The לוים played a huge orchestra while standing on a special set of fifteen steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ties the fifteen physical steps to the fifteen chapters of שיר המעלות in תהלים (chapters 120–134). It also tells us the location: the steps that lead down from עזרת ישראל to עזרת נשים, where the celebration took place.

keyTerms.meaning: Levites, who sang and played music in the Temple
Steps; also 'Ascents', as in שִׁיר הַמַּעֲלוֹת
The Women's Courtyard, where the celebration was held
The Israelites' courtyard, higher up and closer to the היכל

phrases.english: And the Levites with lyres and with harps
and with cymbals and with trumpets
and with countless musical instruments,
standing on fifteen steps
that go down from the Israelites' courtyard to the Women's Courtyard,
corresponding to the fifteen (Songs of Ascents) in Psalms,
phrases.notes: These are תהלים chapters 120–134, each starting with שיר המעלות.

phrases.english: upon which the Levites stand with musical instruments
and recite song.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the לוים's music to the dancing of the חסידים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The לוים played instruments on the fifteen steps, which correspond to the fifteen שיר המעלות.

steps.title: Trumpet blasts as the water procession goes down
steps.stepSummary: Two כהנים with trumpets stood at the upper gate. They blew תקיעה-תרועה-תקיעה at the rooster's call, at the tenth step, in the courtyard and on the ground. They kept blowing until they reached the eastern gate.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two כהנים stood at the Upper Gate that leads down from עזרת ישראל to עזרת נשים, with two trumpets in their hands. When the rooster crowed, they blew תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה. When they reached the tenth step, they blew תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה. When they reached the courtyard, they blew תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה. (When they reached the ground, they blew תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה.) They kept blowing as they walked, until they reached the gate that exits to the east.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now moves from the night of celebration to dawn, when the procession left to draw water for ניסוך המים. Each stage of the walk was marked by a set of trumpet blasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rooster's crow (dawn) marks the end of the night's celebration and the start of the procession. Each stopping point (tenth step, courtyard, ground) gets its own round of blasts, and then the blowing continues all the way to the eastern gate. The line about 'the ground' is in parentheses because it is a variant reading.

keyTerms.meaning: The Upper Gate, at the top of the fifteen steps
The rooster crowed, meaning dawn (some explain it as the Temple crier's call)
They blew a long blast, a broken blast, then a long blast

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the dancing anymore. The scene has moved to dawn and the walk to draw water from the שילוח spring.

phrases.english: And two priests stood at the Upper Gate
that goes down from the Israelites' courtyard to the Women's Courtyard,
with two trumpets in their hands.
When the rooster crowed,
they blew tekia, terua, and tekia.
When they reached the tenth step,
they blew tekia, terua, and tekia.
When they reached the courtyard,
they blew tekia, terua, and tekia.
(When they reached the ground,
phrases.notes: Only some versions have these words, which is why they're in parentheses.

phrases.english: they blew tekia, terua, and tekia.)
They would keep blowing as they walked
until they reached the gate that exits to the east.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the night's celebration to the dawn procession to draw water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Trumpet blasts (תקיעה-תרועה-תקיעה) marked each stage of the procession, continuing until the eastern gate.

steps.title: Turning west and declaring loyalty to God
steps.stepSummary: At the eastern gate they turned to face west, toward the היכל. They declared that their ancestors had turned their backs on the היכל to worship the sun, but 'we, our eyes are to ה''.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they reached the gate that exits to the east, they turned from facing east to facing west and said: Our ancestors who were in this place stood 'with their backs to the היכל and their faces eastward, and they bowed eastward to the sun'. But we, our eyes are to ה'.
steps.whatsHappening: Before leaving the Temple area, the procession turned around to face the היכל. They made a public statement rejecting the idol worship of earlier generations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quoted פסוק is from יחזקאל (8:16). It describes people in the days of the first בית המקדש who faced east, with their backs to the היכל, and bowed to the sun. By physically turning to face west, toward the היכל, the procession acted out the opposite of that sin.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary building of the בית המקדש
But we, our eyes are to God

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the joy of the festival was tied to תשובה: a conscious correction of past sins in the very same place.

phrases.english: When they reached the gate that exits to the east,
they turned their faces from east to west
and said: Our ancestors who were in this place
'with their backs toward the Sanctuary,'
'and their faces eastward,'
'and they bowed eastward to the sun,'
but we, our eyes are to God.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes what happened once the procession reached the eastern gate.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At the eastern gate they faced the היכל and declared their loyalty to ה', in contrast to their ancestors' sun worship.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's version of the declaration
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says they repeated the declaration with a slightly different wording: 'We are to God, and to God are our eyes.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: They would repeat and say: We are to God, and to God are our eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with רבי יהודה's version of what was said at the gate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's wording mentions God's name twice: 'we are to God' and 'to God are our eyes'. This shows that we belong to ה' and look only to Him. The word שונין means they repeated it, so this was said more than once.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא (sage of the משנה) who often gives a differing view

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה describes three parts of the event: the night's joyful celebration, the dawn trumpet procession, and the declaration at the eastern gate rejecting idolatry.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
they would repeat and say:
We are to God, and to God are our eyes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative wording of the declaration in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the declaration was repeated as 'אנו ליה וליה עינינו'.

steps.title: Whoever did not see it never saw true joy or beauty
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא praises three things. Whoever did not see שמחת בית השואבה never saw joy. Whoever did not see ירושלים in its glory never saw a beautiful city. Whoever did not see the בית המקדש built never saw a magnificent building.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: One who did not see שמחת בית השואבה never saw joy in his life. One who did not see ירושלים in its glory never saw a beautiful city. One who did not see the בית המקדש in its built state never saw a magnificent building.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a ברייתא that describes how extraordinary the celebration, the city and the בית המקדש were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is praise, not a legal ruling. The pattern builds outward: first the celebration, then the city it took place in, then the building at the heart of the city. The last line about the building sets up the גמרא's next question.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Our Rabbis taught', which introduces a ברייתא
The Celebration of the Water Drawing

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁלֹּא רָאָה שִׂמְחַת בֵּית הַשּׁוֹאֵבָה —
phrases.english: One who did not see the Celebration of the Water Drawing
never saw joy in his life.
One who did not see Jerusalem in its glory
never saw a beautiful city.

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁלֹּא רָאָה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ בְּבִנְיָנוֹ —
phrases.english: One who did not see the Temple in its built state
never saw a magnificent building.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִי שֶׁלֹּא רָאָה שִׂמְחַת בֵּית הַשּׁוֹאֵבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא expanding on the greatness of the celebration described in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The celebration, ירושלים and the בית המקדש were unmatched in joy and beauty.

steps.title: Which Temple building is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which building of the בית המקדש the ברייתא is praising.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question about the last line of the ברייתא. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were different stages of the בית המקדש: שלמה's first בית המקדש, the plain second בית המקדש built in the time of עזרא, and later rebuilding. The גמרא wants to know which of these the ברייתא calls 'magnificent'.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is it?', a request for clarification

phrases.english: What is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for clarification of 'the Temple in its built state' in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which building of the בית המקדש is referred to as the magnificent structure.

steps.title: It is the building of הורדוס
steps.stepSummary: אביי (or some say רב חסדא) answers that the ברייתא means the building of הורדוס, who rebuilt the second בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said, and some say it was רב חסדא: This is the building of הורדוס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: the magnificent building is the בית המקדש as rebuilt by הורדוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though הורדוס was a wicked king, his renovation made the second בית המקדש extremely beautiful. The words 'ואיתימא' show there is uncertainty about which אמורא said it, אביי or רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And some say', meaning the statement is also attributed to someone else
A leading אמורא (sage of the גמרא) in בבל

steps.whatToRemember: The 'magnificent' בית המקדש praised by the ברייתא is the second בית המקדש as rebuilt by הורדוס.

phrases.english: Abaye said, and some say it was Rav Chisda:
This is the building of Herod.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The magnificent building is the בית המקדש as rebuilt by הורדוס.

steps.title: What materials did הורדוס build with?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what materials הורדוס used to build the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: With what did he build it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just said the praised building was הורדוס's. Now it asks what he built it with, setting up the description that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 named the builder. This question moves from who built it to how it looked. The answer will explain why it was called a magnificent building.

phrases.english: With what did he build it?
phrases.notes: "He" means הורדוס, from the previous step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the identification of the building as הורדוס's.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The building materials of הורדוס's בית המקדש.

steps.title: Built with marble stones
steps.stepSummary: רבא says it was built of green-gray and white marble. Another version says blue and white marble.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: with stones of green-gray marble and white marble. Some say: with stones of blue marble and white marble.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers that the בית המקדש was built of marble stones of different colors. A second version of רבא's words gives slightly different colors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions agree it was marble in two colors. They differ only on whether the darker stone was green-gray or blue. The two colors matter for the next steps, which describe a wave-like look.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say (another version of the report)

phrases.english: Rava said:
With stones of green-gray marble and white marble.
Some say:
phrases.notes: A second version of what was said.

phrases.english: With stones of blue marble and white marble.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two-colored marble stones (green-gray or blue, with white).

steps.title: Rows set in and out to hold plaster
steps.stepSummary: The rows of stone alternated: one stuck out slightly, the next was set in, so plaster would stick.
steps.simpleTranslation: He set one row sticking out and one row set in, so that it would hold the plaster.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes how the stone rows were laid: alternating out and in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plan was to cover the walls with plaster (and then gold). Uneven rows give the plaster something to grip. This sets up the next step about the plan to plate it in gold.

phrases.english: He set one row out and one row in,
so that it would take the plaster.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds detail on how the stones from step 10 were arranged.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The stone rows alternated out and in so plaster would stick.

steps.title: The חכמים tell הורדוס not to cover it in gold
steps.stepSummary: הורדוס wanted to plate the walls with gold, but the חכמים said to leave the stone as it was, because it looked like ocean waves.
steps.simpleTranslation: He planned to plaster it with gold. The חכמים said to him: Leave it, because this way is more beautiful, since it looks like the waves of the sea.
steps.whatsHappening: הורדוס planned to cover the walls in gold, but the חכמים convinced him to leave the bare stone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two colors plus the in-and-out rows made the wall look like rolling waves. The חכמים felt this natural look was more beautiful than gold. This explains why the ברייתא called it a magnificent building.
steps.whatToRemember: הורדוס's בית המקדש was two-colored marble with alternating rows, left uncovered because it looked like the waves of the sea.

phrases.english: He thought to plate it with gold,
the Sages said to him: Leave it,
for this way is more beautiful,
as it looks like the waves of the sea.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the purpose of the plaster setup in step 11 and why it was dropped.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The walls were left as bare marble because they looked like sea waves.

steps.title: רבי יהודה praises the synagogue of אלכסנדריא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי יהודה says whoever did not see the great synagogue of אלכסנדריא never saw the glory of ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יהודה says: Whoever did not see the great synagogue of אלכסנדריא in מצרים never saw the glory of ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another praise in the same style as step 6, now about a huge synagogue in אלכסנדריא. This opens a new description.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It copies the "whoever did not see" pattern from the earlier ברייתא. The next steps will explain what made this synagogue so great.

keyTerms.meaning: A great double-colonnaded hall (the big synagogue)
The glory of the Jewish people

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Whoever did not see the great synagogue
of Alexandria of Egypt,
never saw the glory of Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel praise to the list started in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Alexandria synagogue showed the glory of Israel.

steps.title: The synagogue's huge size
steps.stepSummary: It was like a big hall with rows of columns inside rows of columns, sometimes holding twice the number of Jews who left Egypt.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: It was like a large basilica, a colonnade within a colonnade. Sometimes there were six hundred thousand and another six hundred thousand in it, double the number who left Egypt.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא begins describing the synagogue, starting with its shape and how many people fit inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Columns inside columns made it enormous. The crowd count is compared to יציאת מצרים to show the size: 1,200,000 people, double the 600,000 who left Egypt.

phrases.english: They said: It was like a large basilica,
a colonnade within a colonnade.
At times there were in it
six hundred thousand plus six hundred thousand,
double the number who left Egypt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining the praise in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The synagogue was vast, holding up to 1,200,000 people.

steps.title: Seventy-one golden chairs
steps.stepSummary: There were 71 golden chairs, matching the 71 members of the סנהדרין, each made of a huge amount of gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were seventy-one golden chairs in it, matching the seventy-one of the Great סנהדרין. Each one had no less than twenty-one ten-thousands of talents of gold.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues the description with the golden seats for the elders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number 71 copies the Great סנהדרין, showing the community's honor for Torah leaders. The giant gold amount shows the community's wealth.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיוּ בָּהּ שִׁבְעִים וְאַחַת קָתֶדְרָאוֹת שֶׁל זָהָב,
phrases.english: And there were in it seventy-one golden chairs,

phrases.aramaic: כְּנֶגֶד שִׁבְעִים וְאַחַת שֶׁל סַנְהֶדְרִי גְּדוֹלָה,
phrases.english: corresponding to the seventy-one of the Great Sanhedrin,
each one was no less
than twenty-one ten-thousands of talents of gold.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָיוּ בָּהּ שִׁבְעִים וְאַחַת קָתֶדְרָאוֹת שֶׁל זָהָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues describing the synagogue.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It held 71 golden chairs matching the סנהדרין.

steps.title: Waving a scarf to signal אמן
steps.stepSummary: A wooden platform stood in the middle. The חזן stood on it with scarves and waved one when it was time to answer אמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A wooden platform was in its center. The synagogue attendant stood on it with the scarves in his hand. When it reached the time to answer אמן, he waved the scarf and all the people answered אמן.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains how such a huge crowd knew when to answer אמן, since most could not hear the prayer leader.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hall was too big to hear. So the חזן הכנסת stood high on a בימה and waved a scarf as a signal, and everyone answered אמן together.

keyTerms.meaning: Amen, the response to a ברכה

steps.confusionAlert: Here the חזן is the attendant giving the signal, not the one leading the prayers as in today's usage.

phrases.english: And a wooden platform was in its center,
and the synagogue attendant stood on it
with the scarves in his hand.
And when it reached the time to answer amen,
he would wave the scarf
and all the people would answer amen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Addresses a practical problem caused by the huge size described in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scarf signal let the whole crowd answer אמן together.

steps.title: Seating by trade helped the poor find work
steps.stepSummary: People sat grouped by trade. A poor newcomer could find his fellow craftsmen, and they would help him earn a living.
steps.simpleTranslation: They did not sit mixed. Goldsmiths sat by themselves, silversmiths by themselves, blacksmiths by themselves, coppersmiths by themselves, and weavers by themselves. When a poor man came in, he recognized the people of his trade and went to them. From there came his livelihood and that of his household.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends its description by explaining the seating plan and its kindness to poor strangers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grouping by trade made it easy for a poor stranger to find people in his line of work. They would give him work, which supported him and his family. The glory here is not only gold but also caring for others.
steps.whatToRemember: The synagogue of אלכסנדריא was praised for its size, its wealth, its scarf signal for אמן, and its trade seating that helped the poor find work.

phrases.english: And they would not sit mixed,
rather goldsmiths by themselves
and silversmiths by themselves
and blacksmiths by themselves
and coppersmiths by themselves
and weavers by themselves.
And when a poor man entered there,
he would recognize the members of his trade
and turn to them there.
And from there came his livelihood
and the livelihood of his household.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא's description of the synagogue.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Members sat by trade, so poor newcomers could find work.

steps.title: אביי: אלכסנדר מוקדון killed them all
steps.stepSummary: אביי says all the Jews of that synagogue were killed by אלכסנדר מוקדון.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: And all of them were killed by אלכסנדר מוקדון.
steps.whatsHappening: After all the praise, אביי adds a sad ending: this whole community was wiped out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story turns from glory to tragedy. This raises an obvious question, why such a great community was punished, which the גמרא asks next.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
And all of them were killed by
Alexander of Macedonia.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a tragic end to the community just praised.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The community of אלכסנדריא was destroyed by אלכסנדר מוקדון.

steps.title: Why were they punished?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why such a great community deserved this punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason they were punished?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the punishment, setting up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The community seemed righteous and generous. So the גמרא wants to know what sin caused their destruction.

phrases.english: What is the reason they were punished?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the cause of the tragedy in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The sin that caused the destruction of the community of אלכסנדריא.

steps.title: They broke the ban on returning to Egypt
steps.stepSummary: They were punished for living in Egypt, against the פסוק that says not to return that way again.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they broke this פסוק: "You shall not return that way again," and they went back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that they sinned by settling in Egypt, which the תורה forbids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה (דברים י"ז:ט"ז) commands the Jews not to go back to Egypt. By making Egypt their permanent home, this community broke that command, and that is why they were punished despite their greatness.
steps.whatToRemember: Even the great community of אלכסנדריא was punished because living permanently in מצרים breaks the תורה's command not to return there.
steps.whyThisMatters: This aggadah is a classic source for the איסור of settling in Egypt.

phrases.english: Because they transgressed this verse:
"You shall not again return
that way anymore,"
and they came back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They violated the פסוק forbidding return to Egypt by settling there.

steps.title: אלכסנדר arrives and finds them reading a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: When אלכסנדר מוקדון arrived, he found the Jews reading the פסוק about a nation coming from far away.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he arrived, he found them reading in the ספר תורה: 'ה׳ will bring a nation against you from far away.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story of אלכסנדר מוקדון continues. He arrives in Egypt just as the Jews are reading a frightening פסוק from the curses in the תוכחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line sets up the next step. The פסוק talks about a nation coming from afar 'like a vulture swooping down,' and אלכסנדר is about to see himself in it.

phrases.english: When he (Alexander) came, he found them
that they were reading in the Torah scroll:
"ה׳ will bring upon you a nation from afar"
phrases.notes: דברים כח:מט. The rest of the פסוק says 'as the vulture swoops down.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the punishment that was explained in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אלכסנדר found the Jews reading the פסוק about a distant nation coming upon them.

steps.title: אלכסנדר sees himself in the פסוק and kills them
steps.stepSummary: אלכסנדר reasons that his unusually fast sea voyage proves the פסוק is about him, and he attacks and kills them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Since that man (I) expected to arrive by ship in ten days, and a wind carried it so the ship came in five days, this verse is about me. He fell upon them and killed them.
steps.whatsHappening: אלכסנדר reads the פסוק as a sign about himself, because his trip took half the expected time. He then attacks the Jews and kills them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fast trip seemed to match the 'swooping vulture' in the פסוק, so he concluded Heaven was helping him. This finishes the story begun in step 18 and shows the punishment for living in Egypt being carried out.

keyTerms.meaning: That man (a polite way of saying 'I')

steps.whatToRemember: The story of the great synagogue of אלכסנדריא ends in tragedy. The גמרא linked it to the sin of returning to live in Egypt.
steps.confusionAlert: 'הָהוּא גַּבְרָא' ('that man') is אלכסנדר talking about himself. It is not some other person.

phrases.english: He said: Now, since that man (I)
expected to come by ship in ten days,
and a wind lifted it
and the ship came in five days, (this verse is about me)
he fell upon them and killed them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the story: he interprets the פסוק that was just read and acts on it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אלכסנדר took his fast voyage as proof the פסוק referred to him, and he massacred the community.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: what was the great repair?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's words 'at the end of the first day of יום טוב' and asks what the 'great repair' was.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'At the conclusion of the first day of יום טוב, etc.' (they made a תיקון גדול). What was this תיקון גדול?
steps.whatsHappening: The aggadah section is over, and the גמרא goes back to a new line in the משנה. It asks what 'תיקון גדול' actually means, setting up רבי אלעזר's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the כהנים and לויים went down to the עזרת נשים and made a 'great repair,' but it never explained what that repair was. The גמרא wants the concrete details.

keyTerms.meaning: At the end of the (first) day of the Festival
Etc. (the rest of the quote from the משנה)

phrases.english: "At the conclusion of the Festival day, etc."
What is the 'great repair'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadah about אלכסנדריא and returns to the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What physical change does the משנה's phrase 'תיקון גדול' refer to?

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: a balcony so women sit above
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the walls were once smooth, and they built a balcony so the women sat above and the men below.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: It is like what we learned: The walls were smooth at first. Then they surrounded the courtyard with a balcony, and they arranged that the women would sit above and the men below.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question by quoting a teaching. The 'great repair' was a balcony built around the עזרת נשים, so men and women would be separated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The walls of the עזרת נשים had no ledges at first. Later they added ledges, and each year they laid boards on them to make a balcony. Seating the women up top kept the two groups apart during the celebration.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
It is like that which we learned:
It (the wall) was smooth at first.
And they surrounded it with a balcony,
and they arranged that women would sit above
and men below.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תיקון גדול was building a balcony around the עזרת נשים so women sat above and men below.

steps.title: The two earlier attempts that failed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא describes how they first tried other seating arrangements that did not work, and only then put the women above.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: At first the women were inside and the men outside, and this led to קלות ראש (light-headed behavior). They arranged for the women to sit outside and the men inside, and still it led to קלות ראש. So they arranged that the women would sit above and the men below.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא gives the background to רבי אלעזר's answer. It shows step by step why the balcony became necessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply switching who stood inside and who stood outside did not stop the mixing and improper behavior. Only full separation by height, with women above and men below, solved the problem. That is why the balcony was called a 'great' repair.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'great repair' was complete separation: women in a balcony above, men below. It came only after two weaker solutions failed.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
At first, women were on the inside
and men on the outside,
and they came to light-headed behavior.
They arranged that women would sit outside
and men inside,

phrases.aramaic: וַעֲדַיִין הָיוּ בָּאִין לִידֵי קַלּוּת רֹאשׁ.
phrases.english: and still they came to light-headed behavior.
They arranged that women would sit above
and men below.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on רבי אלעזר's answer by giving the history behind the balcony.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After two failed arrangements, the חכמים placed the women above and the men below to stop improper behavior.

steps.title: How could they change the design of the בית המקדש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: how could they add a balcony, when the בית המקדש's plan was given by ה׳ in writing?
steps.simpleTranslation: How could they do this? Isn't it written: 'All of it is in writing from the hand of ה׳, which He made me understand'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea of adding a balcony. The design of the בית המקדש came from ה׳, so how could people add to it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברי הימים teaches that דוד received every detail of the בית המקדש plan through divine inspiration. That suggests no one may change the structure, so adding a balcony seems forbidden. The answer will come next.
steps.whyThisMatters: This raises a basic principle: the structure of the בית המקדש follows a divine blueprint and cannot be freely changed.

phrases.english: How could one do this?
But isn't it written:
"All of it is in writing from the hand of ה׳, which He made me understand"
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א כח:יט, about דוד giving the plan of the בית המקדש to שלמה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the balcony described in steps 24 and 25 was even permitted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the חכמים added a balcony to the עזרת נשים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The בית המקדש's design was fixed by divine writing, so adding a structure to it should be forbidden.

steps.title: They found a verse and learned from it
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the balcony was not an unauthorized addition. The חכמים found a פסוק and made a דרשה that allowed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: They found a verse and interpreted it, and that is why they built the balcony.
steps.whatsHappening: רב starts answering the קשיא by saying the balcony was based on a פסוק. This line sets up the next amud, where the גמרא quotes that פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קשיא assumed that any change to the בית המקדש's design breaks the written plan from ה׳‎. רב answers that the change itself came from a פסוק, so it is also from the Torah. It is not a human invention added on top of the plan.

keyTerms.meaning: An early אמורא of בבל, the one giving this answer
And they interpreted it (made a דרשה from it)

steps.confusionAlert: רב has not quoted the פסוק yet. Don't look for it in this line. The words 'קְרָא אַשְׁכַּחוּ' only announce that a פסוק is coming, and the גמרא quotes it at the start of the next amud.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key principle: a change to the בית המקדש is allowed only when it has a source in the Torah itself. Human reasoning alone would not be enough.

phrases.english: Rav said:
They found a verse and interpreted it
phrases.notes: The dash shows that the verse itself is about to be quoted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the קשיא of Step 26, which asked how they could add a balcony to a divinely written plan.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Source-based justification: the change itself comes from a פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The balcony looked like a human addition that broke the written divine plan of the בית המקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The balcony came from a דרשה on a פסוק, so it has Torah authority and does not break the plan.
